今天的主题：社交媒体、科技和网络生活。这是雅思 G 类最常见的话题之一：大作文常考「社交媒体让人更亲近还是更孤独」「孩子该不该限制上网」「科技公司该不该为网上的内容负责」；听力和阅读里常出现 platform、content、generate、decline、peak 这类描述趋势的词；口语 Part 1 会直接问 Do you use social media? How has the internet changed your life?。今天是第 6 周第 2 天，强化期继续，每个词后面 ≈ 是同义替换，背的时候连同义词一起记。

例句

  • Most young people get their news from social media platforms rather than newspapers.（大多数年轻人从社交媒体平台而不是报纸上获取新闻。）
  • A large amount of online content is now generated by AI.（现在大量网络内容是由 AI 生成的。）
  • Sales peaked in 2019 and have declined steadily since then.（销量在 2019 年达到顶峰，此后稳步下降。）
  • Technology has evolved so quickly that older people find it hard to keep up.（科技发展得太快，老年人很难跟上。）
  • Online communities can give people a sense of belonging.（网络社区能给人一种归属感。）

同义替换小抄（听力最常见的考法，今天这集几乎都考到了）：

题目写 reached its highest point → 录音说 peaked　|　题目写 fell / decreased → 录音说 went down / declined　|　题目写 centre → 录音说 hub　|　题目写 huge companies → 录音说 behemoths / tech giants　|　题目写 be attracted to → 录音说 gravitate towards / be drawn to　|　题目写 produced by AI → 录音说 AI-generated　|　题目写 developed → 录音说 evolved

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，并能说出至少 15 个词的一个同义替换。再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 platform、content、addiction、privacy 写一句「社交媒体的坏处」，大作文能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Is social media dead?（社交媒体已死？），1 月 8 日这一期。Neil 和 Pippa 聊 AI 时代的社交媒体：网上满是 AI 生成的怪图，社交媒体活跃度 2022 年见顶后一路下降，作家 Kyle Chayka 认为人们会离开科技巨头的大平台，转向更小的网络社区。这集 6 分钟左右，Kyle Chayka 的两段采访语速快、口头语多，最难。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。节目后面照样有一组我按雅思格式出的题（选择 Q1–3 + 笔记填空 Q4–9）。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，像考试一样做下面的 Q1–9，只听一遍，听完点「对答案」。注意题目里的数字和年份（1844、2016、2022），听力里年份经常是定位词；选择题要听清转折点到底是什么。
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Kyle 那两段有很多 like、kind of、I mean，先读懂中文再听。
  4. 第三遍挑 Pippa 解释 behemoth 和 novelty 那段（"Kyle thinks the tech behemoths, meaning large and powerful companies..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：shatter the illusion（打破幻想）、cultural happening（文化热点）、behemoth（巨头）、novelty（新奇玩意儿）、gravitate towards（被……吸引）、Oh man!（哎呀，表示激动）。

Questions 1–9（按雅思格式自编）

Questions 1–3　Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

1 What did the AI-generated photo that Tristan and Asma looked at show?
A a dog dressed up as Jesus　B a man who looked like Jesus and also like his dog　C a man sharing a photo of his breakfast

2 According to a recent report, social media activity
A reached its highest level in 2022 and has fallen since.　B reached its highest level in 2016.　C is still rising among young people.

3 For Kyle Chayka, social media changed when
A AI content first appeared online.　B Twitter became the centre of election debate.　C MySpace stopped being popular.

Questions 4–9　Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

Social media in the age of AI

• The first electronic message (1844) used 4 code, tapped out on a telegraph wire

• Kyle Chayka is a millennial and a digital 5 who writes about social media

• Big tech companies are putting more effort into AI-6 content

• Kyle believes users see this content as a 7 that probably won't last

• He expects people to be attracted to 8 online spaces

• People will connect with individual voices and post 9 in general

答案：1 B　2 A　3 B　4 Morse　5 native　6 generated　7 novelty　8 smaller　9 less。同义替换提示：题目 reached its highest level = 录音 peaked；题目 has fallen since = 录音 has been going down ever since；题目 the centre of election debate = 录音 the hub of election discourse；题目 big tech companies = 录音 tech behemoths；题目 putting more effort into = 录音 leaning into；题目 be attracted to = 录音 gravitating towards。第 1 题 C 是 Pippa 开头说以前大家晒早餐，是干扰项；第 3 题 A 容易误选，Kyle 说的转折点是 2015/2016 年 Twitter 上的选举讨论，不是 AI。

点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Neil：Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.

Neil：大家好，这里是 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是尼尔。

Pippa：And I'm Pippa. Whatever you think of social media, in less than a generation不到一代人的时间里 it has changed the internet. Facebook, Twitter, now known as X, and in the early days早期 MySpace used to be places to post messages to friends or share photos of your breakfast. But with the rise of随着……的兴起 AI, the fun of connecting with friends changed into something much stranger, as Tristan and Asma, presenters of BBC World Service programme The Global Story, found out发现.

Pippa：我是皮帕。不管你怎么看社交媒体，它在不到一代人的时间里就改变了互联网。Facebook、Twitter（现在叫 X），还有早期的 MySpace，过去都是给朋友发消息、晒早餐照片的地方。但随着 AI 的兴起，和朋友联系的乐趣变成了一种怪得多的东西，BBC 国际台节目《The Global Story》的主持人特里斯坦和阿斯玛就发现了这一点。

Tristan Redman：Oh... What is this?

Tristan Redman：哦……这是什么？

Asma Khalid：I think it's a man who's supposed to look like Jesus...

Asma Khalid：我觉得这是一个本来想弄得像耶稣的男人……

Tristan Redman：It's a man who looks a bit like...

Tristan Redman：一个看起来有点像……的男人

Asma Khalid：...who also looks like his dog.

Asma Khalid：……同时也长得像他的狗。

Tristan Redman：He's been AI-ed, right?

Tristan Redman：他被 AI 处理过了，对吧？

Asma Khalid：Has to be AI-ed.

Asma Khalid：肯定是 AI 弄的。

Tristan Redman：He's holding his dog and his face looks like his dog, so he's half Jesus, half dog.

Tristan Redman：他抱着他的狗，脸长得也像那只狗，所以他是半个耶稣、半条狗。

Neil：A half-dog, half-Jesus photo is generated by AI and posted online. It's an example of how the use of AI in social media has evolved演变，发展 so much that today it's hard to know what's created by humans and what's not.

Neil：一张半狗半耶稣的照片由 AI 生成并发到网上。这个例子说明，AI 在社交媒体上的使用已经发展到这种程度：今天已经很难分清什么是人做的、什么不是。

Pippa：In this episode, we'll discuss how social media is changing in the age of AI and, as usual, we'll learn some useful new words and phrases. And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary along with a transcript on our website bbclearningenglish.com.

Pippa：这一集我们来聊聊在 AI 时代社交媒体是怎样变化的，和往常一样，我们也会学一些有用的新单词和短语。别忘了，所有词汇和文字稿都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

Neil：But first, I have a question for you, Pippa. You mentioned MySpace as one of the earliest social media platforms平台, but the first electronic电子的 message was actually sent much earlier, in 1844, using a series of dots and dashes tapped out敲出（信号） by hand on a telegraph电报 wire. So, what was this new form of communication called? Was it:
a) semaphore旗语,
b) dial-up拨号上网, or
c) Morse code?

Neil：不过先问你一个问题，皮帕。你提到 MySpace 是最早的社交媒体平台之一，但第一条电子消息其实早得多，是在 1844 年发出的：人们在电报线上用手敲出一串点和划。那么，这种新的通讯方式叫什么？是 a) 旗语，b) 拨号上网，还是 c) 摩尔斯电码？

Pippa：I think Morse code.

Pippa：我觉得是摩尔斯电码。

Neil：OK. We'll find out the answer later. The introduction of AI has turned some users away from使一些用户离开 social media. Indeed, a recent report found that social media activity peaked达到顶峰 in 2022 and has been going down下降 ever since从那以后一直. Millennial千禧一代（约 1981–1996 年出生） and digital native数字原住民（从小用网络长大的人） Kyle Chayka is a writer specialising专门从事 in social media. He spoke about the problem to Tristan Redmond for BBC World Service programme The Global Story.

Neil：好，答案稍后揭晓。AI 的到来让一些用户离开了社交媒体。事实上，最近一份报告发现，社交媒体的活跃度在 2022 年达到顶峰，此后一直在下降。凯尔·柴卡是一位专门写社交媒体的作家，他是千禧一代，也是「数字原住民」。他在 BBC 国际台节目《The Global Story》里和特里斯坦·雷德曼聊了这个问题。

Tristan Redman：OK. Kyle, was there a moment for you when you felt like social media changed?

Tristan Redman：好。凯尔，有没有哪个时刻让你觉得社交媒体变了？

Kyle Chayka：Oh man!哎呀！（表示激动） I mean... In 2015/2016, I think, in the United States, when Twitter became the hub中心，枢纽 of election discourse讨论，话语, it kind of shattered粉碎，打破 the illusion幻想，错觉 that the internet was a space you could go to, just like, have fun and express yourself and find cool friends and discuss the latest cultural happenings文化热点事件.

Kyle Chayka：哎呀！我是说……我觉得是 2015、2016 年，在美国，Twitter 成了选举讨论的中心，这差不多打破了一种幻想：以为互联网是一个你可以去玩、去表达自己、去结交有趣的朋友、去讨论最新文化热点的地方。

Neil：Kyle uses the informal非正式的 expression, "Oh man!哎呀！（表示激动）" – an exclamation感叹语 showing excitement or enthusiasm热情，激动. He remembers the internet in 2016, when Twitter was full of angry political debate about the US elections. For Kyle, this shattered粉碎，打破 the illusion幻想，错觉 that the internet was fun. If something shatters粉碎，打破 your illusions幻想，错觉, it destroys a false belief you hold, making you realise an unpleasant truth.

Neil：凯尔用了一个口语表达「Oh man!」，这是表示兴奋或激动的感叹语。他回忆起 2016 年的互联网，那时 Twitter 上满是关于美国大选的愤怒政治争论。对凯尔来说，这打破了「互联网很好玩」的幻想。如果某件事 shatters your illusions，就是它摧毁了你原有的错误想法，让你认识到一个不愉快的真相。

Pippa：Kyle thinks social media was friendlier before – an online space to make friends, have fun and discuss the latest cultural happenings文化热点事件. A cultural happening文化热点事件 is an event that embodies体现，代表 the values and interests of a particular group at a particular time in history. For example, the hit television show Game of Thrones was a cultural happening文化热点事件 for millennials千禧一代（约 1981–1996 年出生） in the 2010s.

Pippa：凯尔觉得以前的社交媒体更友好，是一个交朋友、找乐子、讨论最新文化热点的网络空间。cultural happening（文化热点事件）指的是在历史上某个特定时期，体现某个群体价值观和兴趣的事件。比如热播剧《权力的游戏》就是 2010 年代千禧一代的文化热点。

Neil：So, what's the future of social media? Will the amount of AI-generated content continue to grow? Here's Kyle Chayka again, sharing his thoughts with BBC World Service's The Global Story:

Neil：那么，社交媒体的未来会怎样？AI 生成的内容会继续增多吗？再来听听凯尔·柴卡在 BBC 国际台《The Global Story》里分享的看法：

Kyle Chayka：We see the large social networks and the tech behemoths巨头，庞然大物 leaning into大力投入，押注 generated content, and I think users don't actually want that. I think it's a novelty新奇的事物 for now and people will drift away from逐渐远离 it. So instead, I see people gravitating被吸引，倾向于 towards smaller online spaces, connecting more closely with individual voices, like creator types, and just posting less in general总体上.

Kyle Chayka：我们看到大型社交网络和科技巨头都在大力押注 AI 生成的内容，但我觉得用户其实并不想要。我认为它现在只是图个新鲜，人们会慢慢远离它。所以我看到的是，人们反而被更小的网络空间吸引，和一个个具体的人（比如创作者那类人）联系更紧密，而且总体上发帖更少了。

Pippa：Kyle thinks the tech behemoths巨头，庞然大物, meaning large and powerful companies, will continue pushing AI. However, many people want content which is more personal and meaningful有意义的. They think AI is a novelty新奇的事物 – something which is new and unusual and therefore exciting, but which probably won't last.

Pippa：凯尔认为科技巨头，也就是那些庞大而有权势的公司，会继续推 AI。可是很多人想要更个人化、更有意义的内容。他们觉得 AI 只是个新奇玩意儿：新鲜、不寻常，所以让人兴奋，但很可能长久不了。

Neil：Instead, Kyle thinks people will gravitate被吸引，倾向于 towards smaller online communities. If you gravitate被吸引，倾向于 towards something, you are naturally drawn or attracted to it.

Neil：凯尔认为人们反而会被更小的网络社区吸引。如果你 gravitate towards 某样东西，就是你自然而然地被它吸引。

Pippa：Social media has changed fast and is still in motion在变化中. It's come a long way取得长足发展 from the first electronic电子的 messages of 1844 which you mentioned in your question, Neil. So, did I get the correct answer?

Pippa：社交媒体变化很快，而且还在变。比起你问题里提到的 1844 年第一批电子消息，它已经走了很远很远。尼尔，那我答对了吗？

Neil：I asked what this new form of communication was, and you said that it was
c) Morse code. And that, Pippa, is the correct answer. OK. Let's recap回顾，概括 the vocabulary we've learned, starting with the exclamation感叹语, "Oh man!哎呀！（表示激动）" used to show excitement or enthusiasm热情，激动.

Neil：我问的是这种新的通讯方式叫什么，你说是 c) 摩尔斯电码。皮帕，答对了！好，我们来回顾一下今天学的词汇，先是感叹语「Oh man!」，用来表示兴奋或激动。

Pippa：To shatter粉碎，打破 an illusion幻想，错觉 is to destroy someone's misconceptions错误观念, causing them to realise an unpleasant reality.

Pippa：shatter an illusion（打破幻想）就是摧毁某人的错误认识，让他认清不愉快的现实。

Neil：A cultural happening文化热点事件 is an event that embodies体现，代表 the values and interests of a particular social group at a particular time.

Neil：cultural happening（文化热点事件）是在某个特定时期体现某个社会群体价值观和兴趣的事件。

Pippa：A behemoth巨头，庞然大物 is an extremely large and powerful company or organisation.

Pippa：behemoth（巨头）是极其庞大、有权势的公司或机构。

Neil：A novelty新奇的事物 is something which is new and unusual and therefore exciting.

Neil：novelty（新奇事物）是新鲜、不寻常、因而让人兴奋的东西。

小练习

  1. Unemployment ______ in 2020 and has fallen every year since.（达到顶峰）
  2. The number of people buying newspapers continues to ______.（下降）
  3. This software can ______ a short video from a few lines of text.（生成）
  4. Smartphones have ______ a lot since the first iPhone came out.（演变，发展）
  5. For many children, video games are not just a hobby but an ______.（上瘾）
  6. The scandal ______ the illusion that the company cared about its customers.（打破了）
点开看答案

开头那题选 c，摩尔斯电码（Morse code），Pippa 猜对了。填空：1. peaked 2. decline 3. generate 4. evolved 5. addiction 6. shattered

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 1 / Part 3 做准备）：How much time do you spend on social media every day? 用英语说两三句：I spend about ... on ..., mostly to ... / To be honest, I think I ...。Part 3 再想一层：Do you think social media brings people closer together or makes them more isolated?（可以用 platform、community、meaningful、addiction、privacy）
